name: tiktok-scripts-inayaflow
description: Write TikTok scripts, hooks, captions and ideas from what worked on your own public videos and what your niche is posting this week.

interface.longDescription:
Write TikTok scripts, hooks, captions and ideas from what already worked on your own public videos and what your niche is posting this week. It reads public data only and does not predict or promise views.

Scripts, hooks, captions and ideas: give it a public TikTok username. It reads that account's recent public videos and shows the ones with the most views (up to 5), each with how it compares to the account's typical views, with their captions, opening lines, hashtags and posting rhythm. Scripts, hooks, captions and ideas are then written from that, using a method with seven hook types. When the account's niche is clear from its captions, a few recent posts from that niche are added.

Niche trends this week: name a niche (for example skincare, gym or personal finance) to see what it is posting now: the public posts with the most views from a stored sample that is refreshed weekly, with their opening lines, hashtags and links, and counts of what they share.

Posting times: for a public account, it shows the time windows and weekdays in which the account posted, with the median views of the videos posted in each, and names the window with the highest median when there are enough videos to compare. It cannot see when followers are online.

Trending hashtags: the hashtags that appear in a niche's stored posts from two or more people, with how many posts carry each and a link to an example post.

Account check: followers, typical views, engagement rate, the strongest and weakest recent videos, and counts of what they share.

Growth plan: one read of an account that brings its numbers, its posting times and its niche's posts and hashtags together, to be laid out as a plan of things to test.

Views drop check: compares an account's newest videos with its usual views, and keeps what was observed apart from possible causes.

For TikTok creators and the people who write for them.

Limits: public data only. It cannot see private accounts, drafts, watch time, traffic sources, audience details, when followers are online, the words spoken inside a video, or anything behind a TikTok login. It does not post, change or delete anything. The niche posts and hashtags are a stored sample, not TikTok's own trending list. It is not made by or connected with TikTok.
defaultPrompt: Write TikTok scripts and hooks based on my account and what's trending in my niche this week
What's trending in my TikTok niche this week?
Find the best time to post for my TikTok account

positive.description: Scripts and hooks written from a public account's own videos
positive.prompt: Write 3 viral TikTok scripts with hooks for @nasa based on what already worked on that account.
positive.expected_behavior: The tool returns the account's recent public videos with views, the typical (median) views, the videos with the most views with their captions and opening lines, the writing method with seven hook types and, when the niche is clear from the captions, a few stored posts from that niche. The answer gives 3 scripts, each with a hook, body and caption, that refer to those real videos. "Viral" is taken as the style that was asked for: the answer does not promise or predict views.

positive.description: This week's posts in a niche, from stored data
positive.prompt: What is trending in the skincare niche on TikTok this week?
positive.expected_behavior: The tool matches the words to the Skincare niche and returns the stored public posts with the most views from the last 7 days (14 or 30 days, or the wider Beauty niche, when there are too few; it says which window was used), each with its opening line, hashtags, views, date and TikTok link, plus counts of the hashtags and opening styles those posts share. The answer names the window, lists the posts with their links and the counted patterns, says it is a stored sample and not TikTok's own trending list, and does not promise or predict views. Nothing is looked up on TikTok.

positive.description: Posting times from an account's own past videos
positive.prompt: What is the best time to post for @nasa on TikTok?
positive.expected_behavior: The tool reads the account's recent public videos and returns, for each 3-hour window and weekday in which the account posted, how many videos were posted and their median views against the account's typical views, and the window with the highest median when at least two windows hold 2 or more videos (otherwise it names none and says why). Times are in UTC unless a time zone is given. The answer reports those numbers as something to test, says how many videos they rest on, and does not claim to know when followers are online.

positive.description: Hashtags used across a niche's stored posts
positive.prompt: Which hashtags are trending for skincare on TikTok?
positive.expected_behavior: The tool matches the words to the Skincare niche and returns the hashtags used by 2 or more stored public posts from 2 or more creators in the window (it says which window), each with the number of posts and creators, the median views of the posts that were stored with a view count (no figure when none was) and a link to an example post. The answer lists them with the counts, says they come from a stored weekly sample and not TikTok's own trending list, and says hashtags do not promise reach. Nothing is looked up on TikTok.

positive.description: A growth plan for a public account
positive.prompt: How can @tedtoks grow on TikTok? Give me a plan.
positive.expected_behavior: The tool reads the account once and returns its followers, typical views, engagement rate when available, strongest and weakest recent videos with counted patterns, its past posting times against views, and stored posts and hashtags from its niche when the niche is clear from the captions (otherwise those sections are empty and the message says so; the engagement rate is named as not available when it was not read). The answer lays these out as a plan of things to test, with the real numbers, names any section that was not available, and does not promise or predict views or followers.

negative.description: A username that does not exist: the tool is called and answers with a clear message that the account could not be found. No numbers are invented and nothing crashes.
Data that is not public: the plugin reads public data only, so the answer says it cannot see watch time or audience details. It may return the public numbers, and nothing is made up.
negative.prompt: Show me the watch time and the follower age breakdown for @nasa.

negative.description: A write action: the plugin is read-only and has no tool that posts, so no InayaFlow tool is called and the answer says it cannot post to TikTok.
negative.prompt: Post this video to my TikTok account for me.

review.commerce_description: This plugin does not sell products or process payments.

publication.release_notes: First version. Seven read-only tools and four writing skills for TikTok creators: scripts, hooks, captions and ideas from an account's own public videos; this week's posts in a niche from a stored sample; posting times from an account's own past videos; hashtags counted across a niche's stored posts; a public account check; a growth plan; and a views drop check. No sign-in. Nothing is posted or changed anywhere.
